description: As they gather supplies, Bower puts on a boom-mic, clips a radio to his belt, and tests the transmitter. Payton rummages through a drawer, hands him an envelope opener, and says, 'Just in case... there's mail you need to open quickly.' Bower tucks it into a zipper pocket, and a photograph slips out. Payton watches as Bower retrieves it and zips the pocket closed. 'Wife...?' Payton asks. 'Yeah... I think so,' Bower replies. 'Must be newlyweds. How can you forget something like that?' name: Discovering Abandonment and Violence on the Ship
description: Inside the flight deck, rows of empty flight chairs sit in silence, half-filled coffee cups resting on consoles, jackets draped over seat backs as if the crew left in a hurry. The soft blinking of guidance computers fills the dim light. Faint muffled screams echo from deeper within the ship. As the path moves forward, signs of violence become visible—dark smears of blood streak the white walls, and several computer screens lie shattered. The sounds of a heated argument grow louder: panicked voices overlap, one rising in desperate rage. Rounding a corner, a scene unfolds—a trapped officer pounds on the glass of a sealed sleep chamber, shouting in French, his face twisted in terror. On the floor nearby, another officer lies motionless, head bloodied, body twitching. A young corporal moves calmly between terminals, blood streaming from his ears and nose, typing commands with cold precision. The trapped officer screams for him to stop, pleading, warning of disaster. The corporal presses the final key. Alarms blare, lights flash. He closes his eyes, then walks to his own sleep pod, climbs in, and seals the hatch. The trapped officer hammers the glass, screaming in desperation as control panels flare to life. Hydraulics engage. One by one, the sleep pods shift, then launch with a roar of micro-jets.

name: Bower's Awakening and Escape from the Sleep Pod
description: Bower bursts out of his sealed sleep pod, gasping and naked, as the hatch slams open under violent force. He collapses onto the cold floor, his legs buckling beneath him, unable to support his weight. His body glistens with sweat, burns red across his skin, bruises darkening in patches. He struggles to breathe, shouting into the darkness, his voice echoing through a vast, cavernous chamber. The room hums with a low, constant rumble, punctuated by distant creaks and groans of shifting metal. Flickering lights reveal rows of high-tech terminals rising from the floor, shrouded in dust and shadow. Using a glow stick snapped to life, he stumbles back to his pod, tearing at the feeding tubes still attached, sucking liquid from one before retching. He notices two adjacent pods—one empty, labeled 2nd Lt. Cooper, the other occupied by a man under a mask, labeled LT. PAYTON. He calls out, but receives no answer. Returning to his own pod, he sees the name CORPORAL BOWER, a name that means nothing to him. Shivering, he approaches a terminal, tapping the keys, only for dust to rise under his fingers. His hands tremble as he smears the grime away, revealing the label: Elysium - Flight Systems - Operation Terminal #87153-D.
